item.title: D2 WRESTLING: Hanover Area punches ticket to Class 2A final
item.description: HANOVER TWP. — Nate Clime has an important role on the Hanover Area wrestling team. Normally, the freshman runs to the mat for his 107-pound bout in hopes of getting the Hawkeyes off to a strong start. A big spot for the freshman, especially in his first District 2 Class 2A Team Championships. Any pressure? “Not really,” Clime said. “Even though it’s my first year as a freshman, it was pretty important to get the team off to a good start. item.title: HS ROUNDUP: Crestwood boys sweep season series from Hazleton Area
item.description: The Crestwood boys basketball team completed the season sweep of Hazleton Area on Wednesday night. Ayden Agapito and Connor Wagaman each scored 19 points to help Crestwood defeat Hazleton Area, 59-42, on Wednesday night at Crestwood. Miles Metz finished with nine points for Crestwood, while Gio Barna had seven. Crestwood held a 30-19 lead at the half. Yohansal Moran led Hazleton Area with 12 points. item.title: LOCAL COLLEGE: Misericordia men pick up win over Delaware Valley
item.description: The Misericordia men’s basketball team kept pace with Arcadia for the top spot in the MAC Freedom standings. Misericordia raced out to a double-digit halftime lead on its way to a 74-57 win over Delaware Valley on Wednesday night at the Anderson Center. The Cougars rebounded from a loss Saturday at DeSales. item.title: FIELD HOCKEY: Wyoming Area’s Campenni picked for U.S. Under-16 Team
item.description: Ella Campenni never backs down from a challenge, whether it’s playing for the Wyoming Area field hockey team in the Wyoming Valley Conference or with her club team at various sites up and down the East Coast. Campenni, though, took her game to another level when she learned she was selected to the U.S. Under-16 Women’s National Team. item.title: OPINION: Enough with the ‘CEO’ jabs at Eagles coach Nick Sirianni
item.description: The term “CEO head coach,” which is a head coach who doesn’t call plays on either side of the ball, has often been used as a backhanded slight to marginalize coaches’ accomplishments. Exhibit A: Nick Sirianni.
